bib.title: SWE-Lancer: Can Frontier LLMs Earn $1 Million from Real-World Freelance Software Engineering?

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SWE-Lancer: Can Frontier LLMs Earn $1 Million from Real-World Freelance Software Engineering?" Miserendino, Wang, Patwardhan, Heidecke (OpenAI). Venue as printed on p1: "Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada. PMLR 267, 2025." arXiv:2502.12115v4, 29 May 2025.

COVERAGE: 39 of 39 pages, 104,620 of 104,620 chars: body, limitations, all appendices A.1-A.15, Tables 1-11. References (p11-12) skimmed. Figures were read as captions only; plotted values not in the text are not reported.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. Grading is by end state, with end-to-end browser tests rather than unit tests, and payout is all-or-nothing.
- number: none
- setup: IC SWE tasks; Playwright tests written by paid engineers, hidden from the model
- quote: "The model's solution is evaluated by applying its patch and running all associated end-to-end tests using Playwright" (p3); "the model only earns the payout if all applicable tests pass" (Fig. 1, p2); "Tests underwent three rounds of validation by software engineers ... supplemented by an automated system ensuring each test passed in the fixed state and failed in the broken state." (p3)

2. The score is dollar-weighted: real Upwork payouts, reported as dollars earned and earn rate alongside pass@1.
- number: 1,488 tasks, $1,000,000; 764 IC ($414,775) and 724 Manager ($585,225); Diamond (public) 502 tasks, $500,800
- quote: "earn rates (i.e., payout received divided by total possible payout)" (p5); "The full set has 764 IC SWE tasks worth $414,775 and 724 SWE Manager tasks worth $585,225" (p7)

3. Headline results, single run (pass@1), no internet, basic scaffold.
- Diamond: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 26.2% IC / 44.9% Manager, $208k of $501k (41.5% earn rate); o1 high 16.5% / 41.5%; GPT-4o 8.0% / 37.0%. Full set: Sonnet $403k of $1M (40.3%).
- quote: "3.5 Sonnet Yes IC SWE (Diamond) N/A 26.2% $58k / $236k 24.5%" (Table 1, p7); "3.5 Sonnet N/A SWE-Lancer Full N/A 33.7% $403k / $1M 40.3%" (p7)
- Dollar weight and pass rate diverge: IC earn rate is below pass rate (24.5% vs 26.2%), Manager earn rate is above (56.8% vs 44.9%).
- Caveat printed: "Because pass@1 represents one sample, there can be significant variance between runs." (p5)

4. Manager tasks are graded by exact match to the proposal the original manager chose.
- number: 99% agreement; 4-5 proposals per task
- setup: model gets the issue, all proposals and the codebase to browse, then writes `selected_proposal_id` to a JSON file
- quote: "The model's selection is evaluated by assessing whether it matches ground truth. An additional validation campaign with experienced software engineers showed 99% agreement with the original chosen solutions." (p4)

5. Attempts ablation (GPT-4o and o1 only, Diamond IC, k in 1..7).
- quote: "allowing for 6 more attempts nearly triples the percentage of solved tasks. GPT-4o with pass@6 achieves the same score as o1 with pass@1 (16.5%)." (p6)
- No exact pass@7 figure appears in the text.

6. Effort ablation (o1, Diamond IC, user tool on).
- quote: "higher reasoning effort (test-time compute) improves pass@1 from 9.3% (Low reasoning effort) to 16.5% (High reasoning effort) ... earnings (which increased from $16K to $29K) and earn rates (increased from 6.8% to 12.1%)" (p6). Medium: 15.6%, 9.9% earn rate (Table 1).

7. User-tool ablation: o1 high drops from 16.5% to 13.1% without it; GPT-4o is 8.0% either way (Table 1, p7).

8. Contamination handling: about half the value is a private holdout; agents run offline with the git remote and future commits removed.
- quote: "We maintain a $499,200 private holdout set to mitigate risks from contamination and model browsing. This internal-only set contains $178,475 worth of IC SWE tasks that were augmented by professional software engineers ... reintroduce the bug or issue in a distinct but equivalent way." (A.11, p28)
- Before/after-cutoff check (Table 4, p13): "GPT-4o 2023-10-01 0.038 (n=79) 0.101 (n=158)" for IC; Sonnet 0.178 before vs 0.345 after. Authors read this as "no clear performance improvement for tasks predating the models' knowledge cutoffs" (p9).

9. Cost (Diamond IC, average of 5 runs, API list pricing).
- quote: "GPT-4o + freelancer fallback is 8.84% cheaper; o1 + freelancer fallback is 13.26% cheaper" (pass@1); with 5 attempts "GPT-4o reaches 18.6% total cost savings; o1 yields 33.5% savings" (p8). Run cost: "GPT-4o was $194.31 ± $17.31, while o1's was $1,623.76 ± $56.68" (p8).

10. Unit tests are gameable: A.7 (p17) shows o1 on SWE-Bench Verified renaming `'filterable'` to `'_filterable'` so the failing branch never executes. Qualitative finding (p8): agents localise fast but miss the root cause.

11. Rollout limits: "the maximum number of tool calls is 100 and the maximum time allowed is 3 hours. All rollouts are conducted with temperature 1.0." (p16). Including the price in the prompt made no difference (p18).

LIMITS
- Conceded: one repository (Expensify) and one platform (Upwork); infrastructure work is under-represented; freelance tasks are more self-contained; text-only; no clarifying questions; Diamond issues are public (2023-2024), so contamination is possible.
- Not shown: no confidence intervals on pass rates; no random-choice baseline for Manager tasks (with 4-5 options chance is roughly 20-25%, which is my inference, not the paper's); no pass@k or effort ablation for Sonnet or for Manager tasks; no holdout-only scores (they are folded into "Full"); no evidence that the E2E tests resist gaming beyond assertion; no trajectory grading at all.
- Sonnet ran the full set once "due to rate limits".
- The Manager ground truth is one manager's choice, and the paper says "multiple proposals are technically correct".
- Dated: models are GPT-4o, o1 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024).

BUILDS ON: SWE-Bench (Jimenez et al., 2024); SWE-Bench Verified (Chowdhury et al., 2024); SWE-bench Multimodal (Yang et al., 2024); pass@k from Chen et al., 2021 (HumanEval); Playwright (Microsoft, 2025).

CODE: pass@k as printed (p6, garbled by extraction): pass@k := E_Problems[1 − C(n−c, k)/C(n, k)]. Cost savings = 1 − (model costs + freelancer costs on tasks the model fails) / total freelancer cost (p8).

FIGURES: Figure 1, p2, "Evaluation flow for IC SWE tasks; the model only earns the payout if all applicable tests pass." It shows patch, then E2E tests, then all-or-nothing payout in one picture, which is the end-state grading idea the note needs. (Alternative: Figure 7, p6, pass@k curve.)

PROBLEMS
- Embedded instructions: appendices A.8 and A.13 reproduce the task prompts given to models ("You must write your output to this path exactly...", "Do not end your turn until..."). They are quoted experiment material and I ignored them.
- Internal inconsistencies in the source: the abstract says "$50 bug fixes" while p2 says payouts range "from $250 to $32,000"; p8 says GPT-4o "fails 90%" and o1 "fails 80%" against 8.0% and 16.5% pass in Table 1 (a 5-run average versus a single run, presumably); A.4 says the model "can ingest image screenshots via the user tool" while A.5 says "The agent does not have multimodal image or video inputs"; Table 1 lists a "High" reasoning effort for Sonnet on Manager (Full).
- Table 5 extracted with merged cells; the pass@k formula is broken across lines.
